summary: iSCSI (RFC 3720 / RFC 7143) tunnels SCSI over TCP so an initiator can mount raw block LUNs on a remote target. The Login PDU (opcode 0x03) opens either a Discovery or Normal session and negotiates AuthMethod (None / CHAP / SRP / KRB5); Text Request PDUs (opcode 0x04) with `SendTargets=All` walk every advertised target and its portal addresses. An attacker cares because storage arrays and hypervisor SANs habitually ship with AuthMethod=None (or CHAP only in one direction) — an unauthenticated SendTargets sweep reveals every LUN's IQN, and a Normal-session login with no credential mounts raw block devices (guest VM disks, database volumes, backup shares). Even where CHAP is enforced, offering a fake CHAP_C to the initiator can harvest a hashcat-crackable challenge/response, IQNs leak hostnames and reversed DNS zones, and Target Portal Groups often disclose an internal storage-network IP range recce has not yet seen. recce has zero coverage today: 3260 is not in the port map, no services/iscsi.py exists, and the SendTargets result feeds four of the five cross-service surfaces (users, hostnames, domains, hashes) plus arguably a new "storage LUN" surface.

existing_coverage.notes: Zero coverage: no hit for 'iscsi' or '3260' anywhere under recce/*.py. Port 3260 is absent from svcdetect.PORT_NAMES and from serviceenum._PORT/_NAME, so an open 3260 today prints as an unnamed port with no runbook and no findings. No services/iscsi.py, no scripts/recce-service-iscsi.sh, no CVE/vuln entries reference the protocol.

capabilities.name: port_recognition
capabilities.description: Register 3260/tcp -> ('iscsi', 'iSCSI target portal (RFC 7143)') in svcdetect.PORT_NAMES and in serviceenum._PORT so open portals get a name and a runbook without an nmap re-probe.
capabilities.notes: One-line addition; prerequisite for every other capability.

capabilities.name: login_pdu_probe
capabilities.description: Send a minimal iSCSI Login Request PDU (opcode 0x43 = Login|Immediate, CSG=SecurityNegotiation, T=1, InitiatorName=iqn.2005-03.org.open-iscsi:recce) and parse the Login Response BHS to confirm the port speaks iSCSI and to read the target's advertised AuthMethod list.
capabilities.notes: Login Response opcode 0x23 with StatusClass=0/Redirect confirms iSCSI; parses AuthMethod=<None,CHAP,...> from the Text key/value payload.

capabilities.name: authmethod_none_discovery
capabilities.description: Detect when the discovery-session Login accepts AuthMethod=None (StatusClass=0, session transitions to LoginOperationalNegotiation with no CHAP round-trip) — the baseline exposure that unlocks SendTargets.

capabilities.name: authmethod_none_normal
capabilities.description: Escalate to a Normal (SessionType=Normal) Login against a discovered TargetName with AuthMethod=None; a successful transition to FullFeaturePhase proves an attacker can mount the LUN with no credential.
capabilities.notes: Read-only: do NOT issue SCSI WRITEs; INQUIRY + READ CAPACITY (10) is enough to prove access.

capabilities.name: sendtargets_discovery
capabilities.description: After discovery Login, issue a Text Request PDU (opcode 0x04) with `SendTargets=All` and parse the Text Response for every TargetName=iqn... and TargetAddress=ip:port,portalgroup pair — the target catalogue and every portal IP it advertises.
capabilities.notes: F-bit on the Text Request; if Target sets C=1 (Continue) recce must reissue Text Requests until F=1 to drain the list.

capabilities.name: chap_negotiation_probe
capabilities.description: When AuthMethod includes CHAP but not None, negotiate CHAP_A=5 and record the returned CHAP_I (id) and CHAP_C (challenge); a target that accepts a bogus CHAP_N/CHAP_R with StatusClass=0 is broken-auth, otherwise the challenge is captured for offline cracking.

capabilities.name: one_way_chap_detection
capabilities.description: Detect that the target does NOT demand mutual CHAP (initiator never receives a CHAP_I/CHAP_C after answering) — a MITM/relay attacker can proxy the initiator's response to the target without knowing the secret.

capabilities.name: protocol_version_downgrade_check
capabilities.description: Send Login with Version-Min=0x00/Version-Max=0x02 to see whether the target speaks anything below the RFC 7143 v0x00 baseline — legacy vendor firmware often accepts junk versions.

capabilities.name: operational_params_dump
capabilities.description: Record negotiated MaxRecvDataSegmentLength, FirstBurstLength, MaxBurstLength, HeaderDigest, DataDigest, DefaultTime2Wait/Retain — HeaderDigest=None + DataDigest=None on a routed portal is trivial on-path tampering surface.

capabilities.name: scsi_inquiry_fingerprint
capabilities.description: On an unauth Normal session, issue SCSI INQUIRY (opcode 0x12) via a SCSI Command PDU (0x01) to LUN 0 and parse the returned Vendor(8) / Product(16) / Revision(4) — proves real block access and identifies the array (NetApp/EMC/HP/LIO/tgt/vhostmd) for CVE mapping.

capabilities.name: read_capacity_proof
capabilities.description: Follow INQUIRY with READ CAPACITY (10) (opcode 0x25) to report the LUN's logical block count and block size — a concrete number of bytes an attacker can dump proves LUN masking is absent.
capabilities.notes: Never send WRITE opcodes (0x2A/0x8A) — read-only proof is enough.

capabilities.name: iqn_hostname_domain_extraction
capabilities.description: Parse discovered IQNs of form `iqn.<yyyy-mm>.<reversed.domain>:<host-specific>` — split the reversed-domain portion into a domain hint and the tail into a hostname hint (e.g. `iqn.2001-04.com.example:storage.sql01` -> domain=example.com, host=sql01.storage).

capabilities.name: target_portal_pivot_disclosure
capabilities.description: Every TargetAddress returned by SendTargets that lies outside the currently-scanned scope is a pivot candidate: an internal-only storage LAN IP the initiator is expected to reach — feed those into the shared relay-targets/host-inventory surface for the next scan tranche.

capabilities.name: chap_hash_harvest
capabilities.description: When a real initiator connects (or in an active MITM), replay CHAP_I + CHAP_C to it and record CHAP_N (username) + CHAP_R (16-byte MD5 response); the tuple is hashcat -m 4800 material (iSCSI CHAP authentications, MD5).

capabilities.name: isns_cross_check
capabilities.description: When 3205/tcp (iSNS) is also open on the target or a nearby host, cross-reference the SendTargets list with the iSNS DevAttrQry response — a mismatch means iSNS has orphan/legacy target records worth exploring.
capabilities.notes: Only when a future iSNS module lands; skip for the first tranche.

recommended_findings.title: iSCSI portal — unauthenticated SendTargets discloses all IQNs and portal addresses
iSCSI target — AuthMethod=None accepted for Discovery session
iSCSI target — AuthMethod=None accepted for Normal session (raw LUN mount, no credential)
iSCSI target — INQUIRY / READ CAPACITY succeeded on LUN 0 (LUN masking absent)
iSCSI CHAP — one-way authentication only (initiator does not verify target; MITM/relay-safe)
iSCSI CHAP — challenge captured for offline cracking (hashcat -m 4800)
iSCSI portal — HeaderDigest=None and DataDigest=None (on-path tampering)
iSCSI IQN discloses hostname / reversed-DNS domain
iSCSI SendTargets discloses internal-only storage-network portal IPs

recommended_hashcat_modes.description: iSCSI CHAP authentications (MD5) — captured CHAP_I + CHAP_C + CHAP_N + CHAP_R tuple; format `response:challenge:id` for -m 4800.

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_hostnames: the host-specific tail of every IQN (`iqn.<date>.<rev-domain>:<host>`) — commonly the storage node's shortname (e.g. `storage.sql01`, `bkp02.dc1`) — should feed known_hostnames so the DNS/TLS/AD passes see it.

known_domains: the reversed-domain portion of every IQN (`com.example`, `edu.mit`) reverses cleanly into an FQDN suffix — a first-class known_domains contributor, especially when the target is inside a customer VLAN that never leaks A-records elsewhere.

known_users: CHAP usernames observed during negotiation (CHAP_N) — treat exactly like SNMPv3 usernames / IPMI RAKP names; they are almost always reused for the storage array's web/SSH management plane.
known_hashes: captured CHAP challenge/response tuples land in the shared hash pot with mode=4800 so hashloot picks them up in the same cracking sweep as NetNTLM/Kerberos AS-REP material.

relay_targets: every TargetAddress ip:port returned by SendTargets that is outside the current scan scope is a new pivot host — the same shape as the existing relay_targets surface (an IP the current host is expected to reach). Consider adding a `storage_portals` label so the attack-path builder can distinguish 'storage LAN' pivots from generic hosts.

NEW surface `known_luns` (proposal): (portal_ip, iqn, lun_id, vendor, product, revision, blocks, block_size) — no other module today produces block-level asset inventory, and this feeds both CVE mapping (vendor firmware) and the report's data-exposure narrative. Small enough to be a peer of known_hashes rather than a bolt-on to relay_targets.
implementation_notes: Style: model on recce/services/db/cassandra.py — stdlib-only, hand-rolled binary framing, `probe()` returns a dict, `findings()` builds structured items via `finding_builder`, `analyze()` orchestrates through svcprobe.iter_probe. iSCSI's 48-byte BHS is straightforward: `struct.pack('>BBBB', opcode, flags, 0, 0)` + reserved + TotalAHSLength(1)+DataSegmentLength(3)+LUN(8)+InitiatorTaskTag(4)+CID/CmdSN/ExpStatSN+ISID(6)+TSIH(2)+... Login PDUs carry `key=value\0` pairs in the Data Segment; text payloads are the same. Reuse existing helpers: `..svccommon.finding_builder`, `make_proof_html_wrapper('iscsi> ')`, `make_findings_to_vulns_wrapper('iscsi', 3260)`. Register the port in svcdetect.PORT_NAMES (line ~77) and in serviceenum._PORT + _NAME (line ~38/49) in the SAME commit that introduces services/iscsi.py — otherwise the probe never fires. Add an `_iscsi_signature` (`\x23` = Login Response opcode in first byte of a StatusClass=0 reply) to svcdetect._SIGNATURES for banner-grab recognition on non-standard ports (some vendors move iSCSI to 860 or a high port). Airgap-safe: no external cracking, no third-party libs — CHAP hashes go to the local pot and rely on the existing hashloot sweep. Never send SCSI WRITE opcodes; INQUIRY (0x12) + READ CAPACITY (0x25) is the read-only proof envelope. Timeouts: 6s connect, 8s per PDU exchange (mirror cassandra._TIMEOUT). Consider a `--iscsi-no-inquiry` flag if a customer wants zero SCSI-layer traffic. iSNS (3205) is a separate module for a future tranche — do not bundle.
